His books include memoirs and an account of modern Greek politics.

long_biography.plain_text:
Greek columnist Taki Theodoracopulos turned to journalism after a decade on the European tennis circuit. William F. Buckley hired him as a foreign correspondent for National Review, but writing in English required extensive editing. Buckley encouraged him to learn by listening closely to well-spoken English, while literary friendships gave him opportunities to meet and interview established writers.

His financing of The American Conservative involved a limited commitment, with Scott McConnell handling recruitment and production. A small staff and inexpensive newsprint kept costs down, and Taki contributed a column to every issue. After fulfilling his initial funding commitment, he transferred most of his ownership to McConnell.
